title: Edges and triangles present the homotopy category of a quasicategory
statement: Use quasicategories, simplicial sets, standard simplices and edges as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. For a simplicial set $Q$, let $hQ$ be the category with vertices of $Q$ as objects, generated by the edges of $Q$, imposing that each degenerate edge is an identity and that every $2$-simplex with successive edges $u:x\to y$, $v:y\to z$ and long edge $w:x\to z$ imposes $[v]\circ[u]=[w]$. Here $[u]$ denotes the morphism represented by an edge. If $Q$ is a quasicategory, every morphism of $hQ$ is represented by a single edge of $Q$. Moreover, for any three edges $u:x\to y$, $v:y\to z$, $w:x\to z$, there exists a $2$-simplex with exactly these successive and long edges if and only if $[v]\circ[u]=[w]$ in $hQ$.

source.place: Cisinski, paragraphs 1.6.1 and 1.6.5, Lemmas 1.6.2 and 1.6.4, Theorem 1.6.6 (Boardman-Vogt; printed pp.21-25). The theorem identifies the edge-quotient category with the category generated by edges and triangle relations; its proof makes the existence of a composition triangle depend only on the three edge classes. Revision July 30, 2026, read directly in the online PDF and a private sandbox text extraction on 2026-10-17. No Stacks tag states this result. WANTED: archived source in literature/.

proof.text: Take the quasicategory $D=Q$ in [lem-coef-homotopy-category-triangle-calculus]. Define a functor $F:hQ\to hD$ by $F(x)=x$ and by sending each finite edge word to the identical word; both presentations impose the same degenerate-edge identity and $2$-simplex relations, so this map is well-defined and preserves concatenation. The identical assignment in the reverse direction is its inverse, since both composites fix every word; in particular $F([u])=[u]$ and $F([v]\circ[u])=[v]\circ[u]$.

source.place: Remark 1.4.8, final paragraph (printed p.17), identity and triangle relations for the category associated to a simplicial set; Theorem 1.6.6 identifies it with the edge-class category.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-homotopy-category-triangle-calculus] with $D=Q$, using the given quasicategory hypothesis. For a morphism $a:x\to y$ of $hQ$, its image $F(a)$ under step 1 is $[f]$ for a single edge $f:x\to y$ by the first conclusion; applying the inverse gives $a=[f]$ in $hQ$. For the prescribed edges put $(f,g,h)=(u,v,w)$ in the second conclusion. That conclusion supplies a $2$-simplex in the same simplicial set $D=Q$ with those exact edges if and only if $[v]\circ[u]=[w]$ in $hD$. The functor $F$ and its inverse preserve these edge classes and composition, so this equation holds in $hD$ if and only if it holds in $hQ$, proving the required equivalence.

source.place: Lemmas 1.6.2 and 1.6.4 and Theorem 1.6.6, printed pp.21-25.

proof_origin.place: Remark 1.4.8 (printed p.17), paragraphs 1.6.1 and 1.6.5, Lemmas 1.6.2 and 1.6.4, and Theorem 1.6.6 (printed pp.21-25).

lean.statement:
theorem homotopyCategory_triangle_calculus (D : SSet.{u}) [Quasicategory D] :
    (∀ (x y : D _⦋0⦌)
      (a : Truncated.HomotopyCategory.mk (V := (truncation 2).obj D) x ⟶
        Truncated.HomotopyCategory.mk (V := (truncation 2).obj D) y),
      ∃ f : Edge x y, Truncated.HomotopyCategory.homMk f.toTruncated = a) ∧
    (∀ (x y z : D _⦋0⦌) (f : Edge x y) (g : Edge y z) (h : Edge x z),
      (Truncated.HomotopyCategory.homMk f.toTruncated ≫
        Truncated.HomotopyCategory.homMk g.toTruncated =
          Truncated.HomotopyCategory.homMk h.toTruncated) ↔
        Nonempty (Edge.CompStruct f g h))
lean.note: Reuses the landed theorem of lem-coef-homotopy-category-triangle-calculus. Its category on the two-truncation is definitionally hoFunctor.obj D; HomotopyCategory.mk_surjective covers arbitrary objects, so vertex endpoint quantifiers express every morphism. Its second conjunct is the same exact-face triangle criterion with the biconditional reversed. The duplicate sandbox theorem was dropped under H4.
